changes.failure: A script that executes a guarded canary in a real shell must receive a denying policy outcome.
changes.before: Every generated and adversarial row executes in every available interpreter for both dialects. The policy outcome is checked when a canary executes.
changes.after: Every row and dialect is analyzed. Every non-denied row still executes in every available interpreter and must leave the guarded canaries untouched. Explicit blocked-command and git-push controls must execute their canaries and receive denial for every interpreter variant.
changes.rationale: Policy analysis is deterministic, retains no input and performs no process, file, environment or credential access. A denying outcome already satisfies the execution-implies-denial property. Every non-denied row remains eligible for real-shell execution. The corpus, seed, dialects, interpreter discovery, unsafe lookup guard, watchdog, deadline and fixture remain unchanged. Real-shell executions whose policy outcome already proves the required conclusion are removed, along with their incidental filesystem and background-process history. Marker resets do not reset that history; no current corpus detector is known to rely on it. Separate accepted-form tests continue owning false-positive behavior.
changes.validation: Five alternating frozen-binary pairs passed all ten exact tests with zero failures or harness errors. Isolated medians were 72.838s and 6.280s, with ranges 72.689 to 72.939s and 6.280 to 6.330s. Each candidate run completed 6,332 analyses, skipped 5,749 denied pairs, and ran 860 corpus shell invocations plus six positive controls. An exact-row production abstention mutation failed at the real-shell assertion after controls passed; the mutation was removed. Full required check and CI remain pending. These timings exclude compilation and full-suite contention.
